newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Banque Audi eurobond heavily subscribed.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Banque Audi eurobond heavily subscribed.

text.p: Lebanon's Banque Audi launched a heavily-oversubscribed $100 million eurobond on Wednesday, bringing to $320 million the total funds Lebanese commercial banks have raised on the international debt market since June.
Market sources said the five-year issue, lead managed by Merrill Lynch International, attracted firm investor demand totalling more than $250 million.
The issue was raised to $100 million from an initial indicated size of $75 million.
The sources said the eurobonds were placed 75 percent with institutional investors and sold 40 percent in the United States, 40 percent in Europe and 20 percent in the Middle East.
"This is the first Lebanese institution to tap into the real institutional investors. It is a real accomplishment," a market source said.
The issue was priced at 99.824 with a coupon of 9.375 percent to yield 315 basis points over the corresponding five-year U.S. Treasury Notes, Merrill Lynch said in a statement.
Beirut bankers said the price was a positive indication of foreign investor acceptance of Lebanon risk.
"The pricing is fine. It looks very good for them," a banker told Reuters.
"They have priced the bonds at a relatively low margin and they were still well received, so this is good for the Lebanese market.
"It is positive in the sense of the risk perception of foreign investors towards Lebanon," the banker added.
Banque Audi is the fifth Beirut bank to issue Euronotes since Lebanese banks began tapping the international debt market in June.

Merrill Lynch said the issue launched a $200 million Euronote programme. It is intended to set a benchmark that will enable Audi to access the international markets for future tranches with maturies ranging from one to 10 years, it added.

Audi, one of several leading Beirut banks moving into consumer financing, will use the proceeds to enhance its ability to meet a growing demand for medium- and long-term financing in Lebanon, Merrill Lynch said.
It said the issue marked a number of firsts for the Middle East, including:
- the first five-year issue by a private sector Lebanese borrower,
- the first Lebanese issue marketed and sold into the United States through a 144A tranche,
- the first Euro-medium term note (EMTN) programme established by a Lebanese or Arab issuer, and
- the first London Stock Exchange listing for a Middle Eastern issuer.
Market sources said the bonds would be listed on the London Stock Exchange after the issue closes, expected November 5.

Banque Audi, which raised equity capital on the international markets through a Global Depository Receipts (GDR) issue last year, is Lebanon's third largest bank by assets and deposits and the second largest in shareholders' equity.
Its total assets at June 30 were $1.5 billion and Capital Adequacy ratio was 15.1 percent. The bank posted profits of $10.2 million and $18.9 million in 1994 and 1995 respectively.
